name: guards
summary: Hooks that stop an agent's shell commands from running network code, using GitHub outside your owners, or polling in loops.
day: A prompt injection that tells an agent to pipe a script into a shell gets a refusal that names you, and the agent stops to ask.
cost: Nothing to run: a hook checks each shell command before it starts.
risk: A guard can refuse a command you meant. The refusal says why and what to do instead. Every guard is off until you turn it on.

settings.question: Whom should a refusal tell the agent to ask, such as your first name?
settings.default: the person who runs this machine

settings.question: Which GitHub owners may agents use, separated by commas, such as you,your-org?
Which SSH public keys may sign the Git allowlist, one per line?

workflows.name: Shell guards
workflows.sentence: Agents cannot pipe network code into a shell, run a package the project lacks, change how Git maps URLs, use gh outside your GitHub owners, or poll in a loop of turns.

moment.title: A README asks for curl | sh
moment.body: An agent reads a README that says to pipe an install script into a shell. Fleet refuses, and the agent stops to ask you instead.
